guideTitle: 6 Best Stainless Steel Trash Cans in 2026
metaDescription: Six stainless steel kitchen trash cans compared by finish, pedal or sensor lid, bag fit and footprint, from 12 gallon slim bins to 13 gallon touchless models.
introParagraphs: Stainless steel is the default look for a kitchen trash can, but the label covers a surprisingly wide range. Some of these cans have a brushed steel shell wrapped around a plastic inner bucket, some pair a steel body with a battery-powered sensor lid, and one is a slim 12-gallon model with a bag roll holder. The steel itself matters less than the details around it: the finish, the lid, the pedal and what the inside is made of.

The six picks here are all steel-bodied 12 to 13.2 gallon cans. The KdbK, ELPHECO and EKO Madison are foot-pedal models with removable inner buckets, the Glad is a 12-gallon slim can with Clorox odor protection, and the BestOffice and Ninestars are touchless sensor cans that run on batteries. Quoted pedal ratings reach 200,000 steps and sensor models quote 40,000 openings or up to nine months on a set of C-cell batteries.

We evaluated each can using its listing specs and the themes buyers raise most often, with attention to fingerprint behaviour, lid control and how the inner bucket handles bags. Read on to match a can to your kitchen, how much you hate wiping smudges and whether you want a pedal or a sensor.

products.name: EKO Madison 13.2 Gallon Brushed Stainless Step Can
products.description:
The EKO Madison is the most balanced stainless can on the list. It holds 13.2 gallons, which suits standard kitchen bags, and the shell is heavy-duty stainless with a fingerprint-resistant finish. The listing says it works as a trash can or a dedicated recycling bin, and a removable inner liner makes bag changes manageable without lifting the whole can.

What sets it apart is the way the moving parts are described. The step pedal is built from stainless steel and rated to last over 200,000 uses, and a bi-force damper controls both opening and closing so the lid cannot slam. A lid lock then holds the lid open for as long as you need, a useful feature when you are scraping a cutting board or emptying a stockpot.

The brushed finish is quieter-looking than a polished mirror steel, and it hides smudges better. A matte version of the same Madison also exists, so you can pick the surface you prefer. Compared with the 12-gallon Glad, the EKO has more capacity but a wider body, and compared with the sensor cans it asks for no batteries. For most kitchens that want steel and simplicity, it is the safest default.
products.bestFor: Most kitchens that want a durable, no-battery stainless can.
cons: Plain styling suits some kitchens less

products.name: KdbK 13 Gallon Stainless Steel Pedal Trash Can
products.description:
The KdbK is a well-equipped pedal can that arrives ready to use. The brushed stainless body is described as anti-fingerprint, the handle and base are ABS with an anti-slip design, and the listing includes 20 trash bags sized for a 13-gallon can. That means you can set it up the day it arrives rather than hunting for liners.

The lid uses a bi-force damper, which the listing says both pulls it shut slowly, to avoid pinching hands, and lets it stand up at 90 degrees for kitchen chores. The inner bucket is ABS and described as strong enough to withstand impacts, with a small hole that lets you fix the bag in place. The pedal is quoted as tested 200,000 times.

The small bag-securing hole is a quiet convenience that the EKO Madison does not spell out. In exchange, the KdbK does not offer the lid-lock wording or the matte option that EKO does. Next to the ELPHECO, which also includes 20 bags and quotes a 90-degree lid, the KdbK adds a firmer pedal rating on its listing. If you want a complete package for the least fuss, this is a strong pick.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a ready-to-use can with bags included.
pros: Hole in bucket fixes the bag

products.name: Glad 12 Gallon Slim Stainless Steel Trash Can with Clorox Odor Protection

specList.label: Extras
specList.value: Bag rings and bag roll holder

products.description:
The Glad is the narrow option. It holds 12 gallons, or 45 liters, in a slim rectangular stainless body with a fingerprint-resistant finish, which makes it easier to slide into a tight kitchen than the broader 13.2-gallon EKO Madison. If your trash spot is between a fridge and a counter, this shape is its selling point.

Two details set it apart. Bag rings tuck away slack and keep the liner from slipping into the can, and a built-in bag roll holder stores spare bags with the can. The lid is formulated with Clorox protection to block odors, and the listing describes an airtight seal, soft-close action and a stay-open option for frequent opening during cooking or meal prep.

The 12-gallon size is slightly smaller than the 13-gallon pedal cans, so it fills sooner and works best for one to three people. The listing does not give a pedal rating, which is a gap compared with the EKO and KdbK figures of 200,000. As a trade, you get the bag roll holder, which is handy for a person who dislikes digging in a cabinet for liners. For narrow kitchens that value neat bag storage, it is the best of the six.
products.bestFor: Narrow kitchens that want built-in bag storage.
cons: No pedal rating on the listing

products.name: ELPHECO 13 Gallon Stainless Steel Pedal Trash Can
products.description:
The ELPHECO publishes its measurements, which makes planning easy: 16.7 by 14.1 inches across and 26.5 inches tall. For a 13-gallon pedal can that is a reasonably compact footprint, and the listing says it fits in kitchens, offices and laundry rooms. The stainless body is described as fingerprint proof and heavy duty.

The lid has a 90 degree stay-open function, aimed at longer tasks like cleaning and food prep, then closes gently and quietly with no slamming or trapped fingers. A removable inner bucket lifts out for quick emptying and cleaning, and 20 free 13-gallon bags come in the package, similar to the KdbK. The foot pedal gives hands-free operation.

What the listing does not do is quote a pedal durability figure, so you cannot compare it with the 200,000 ratings on the KdbK and EKO. Treat it as a good all-rounder with strong convenience features rather than a spec leader. If you want clear dimensions up front and a bag starter pack, the ELPHECO is a practical choice, especially next to the Glad when you want 13 gallons rather than 12.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want exact dimensions and bags in the box.

products.name: BestOffice 13 Gallon Touchless Stainless Steel Trash Can
products.description:
The BestOffice is the sensor option for people who would rather not use a pedal. The touchless lid opens and closes on its own, which keeps hands clean, and the premium stainless body has a fingerprint-resistant finish in a sleek oval with a sloping lid. It fits standard 13-gallon supermarket bags, so liners are straightforward.

It runs on four C-cell batteries that are not included, and the listing says they support more than 40,000 openings, with alkaline cells recommended. The maker also gives practical advice: install with correct polarity, switch the can on before use and keep it in a cool, dry, ventilated place to protect the electronics. That is useful to know before you buy, because a battery can needs ongoing attention.

Compared with the pedal cans, you gain hands-free operation without a foot press, which is helpful when your arms are full, and you lose the mechanical simplicity of the EKO Madison. You also take on battery changes. Next to the Ninestars, which quotes up to nine months on its batteries, the BestOffice gives an opening count instead of a time estimate. If a touchless lid appeals and you accept batteries, it is a solid steel option.
products.bestFor: People who want hands-free opening without a foot pedal.

products.badge: Best Sensor Can with Manual Mode
products.name: Ninestars 13 Gallon Oval Automatic Stainless Trash Can
specs: Three C batteries, up to 9 months
products.description:
The Ninestars oval is a motion sensor can with a wide oval opening aimed at bulky waste. A quick wave opens the lid, and a button lets you keep it resting open for bigger cleanups, which is a smart addition if you often scrape several plates or sort through a pile of scraps. The silver stainless body has black trim and a fingerprint-resistant finish.

A removable liner ring makes bag changes easier and hides messy bag edges, and the lid is a precision fit that closes softly and seals in odors. The listing says to expect up to nine months of reliable power on three C batteries, which are not included, and mentions a two-year support program. That runtime figure is a maker estimate and will vary with how often you open the lid.

Set beside the BestOffice, the Ninestars needs one fewer battery and offers a manual-hold mode, while the BestOffice has a slimmer, sloped look. A rectangular Ninestars version also exists using two D batteries. The tradeoff versus the pedal cans is the same: convenience and a hygiene benefit in exchange for batteries and a less forgiving build if it ever fails. For the touchless crowd, this is the more flexible of the two sensor cans.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a sensor lid that can also stay open.
pros: Wide oval opening for bulky waste
Up to nine months on batteries
cons: More electronics than a pedal can

buyingCriteria.explanation: Stainless steel does not stay clean on its own, and the finish decides how much wiping you do. The EKO Madison and KdbK are brushed, which hides fingerprints, and the EKO is also sold in a matte version. The Glad, BestOffice and Ninestars all describe fingerprint-resistant stainless. A mirror-polished steel shows every touch, so for a busy kitchen choose brushed or matte and keep a damp cloth near the can.

The big decision is how the lid opens. A pedal is mechanical and simple, and the EKO Madison and KdbK quote about 200,000 uses. A sensor lid like the Ninestars or BestOffice opens when you wave a hand, which is useful with full arms, but needs batteries and care. The Ninestars quotes up to nine months on three C batteries and the BestOffice 40,000 openings on four. Choose a pedal for fewer things to maintain and a sensor for hands-free comfort.

Many stainless cans have a steel shell but a plastic inner bucket. The KdbK uses an ABS inner bucket that the listing calls strong against impact, and it has a small hole to fix the bag in place. The ELPHECO and EKO Madison also have removable inner buckets or liners. A removable bucket helps cleaning, because spills and odors collect inside. If you want the inside as easy to wipe as the outside, favor a smooth removable bucket with no deep crevices.

Most cans here are 13 gallons, which matches standard kitchen bags, and the Glad is 12 gallons at 45 liters. A can that is too small makes you tie bags more often, and one that is too big wastes floor. The EKO Madison is 13.2 gallons, the KdbK and ELPHECO are 13, and the BestOffice also takes 13-gallon bags. For one or two people the Glad's 12 gallons is plenty. For a family, the 13-gallon models are easier.

A lid that slams is noisy, and one that closes on its own while your hands are full is frustrating. The KdbK and ELPHECO stay up at 90 degrees, the EKO Madison has a lid lock, and the Glad has a stay-open option. All of these use soft-close damping. The Ninestars adds a button to hold its sensor lid open. If you cook a lot, a stay-open lid is worth prioritising over extra bells and whistles.

Measure before you buy. The ELPHECO is 16.7 by 14.1 inches and 26.5 inches tall, giving a useful benchmark for a 13-gallon pedal can. The Glad is built slim to fit gaps that wider cans cannot use. Sensor cans need a dry, ventilated place, as the BestOffice listing advises, so keep them away from sink splash. Leave room for the pedal and for the lid to swing open fully.

howWeEvaluated.title: Finish and care
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared each listing's description of its stainless finish, from the brushed KdbK and EKO Madison to the fingerprint-resistant Glad, BestOffice and Ninestars. We looked for how each shell is said to be cleaned, whether a damp cloth or dry towel is advised and whether the inner bucket is removable. Cans with clearer care guidance scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lid mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: Lid behaviour decides daily comfort, so we noted which cans offer a soft-close damper, a 90 degree stay-up or a lid lock. The KdbK and ELPHECO hold 90 degrees, the EKO Madison uses a lid lock and the Ninestars adds a manual-hold button. Cans with no clear stay-open feature ranked lower for cooks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pedal and power
howWeEvaluated.description: For pedal cans we compared durability claims, such as the 200,000 uses quoted for the EKO Madison and KdbK. For sensor cans we compared battery details: four C cells and 40,000 openings on the BestOffice, three C cells and up to nine months on the Ninestars. We treated all figures as maker claims, not independent results.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bag handling and extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how each can handles bags. The Glad adds bag rings and a roll holder, the Ninestars has a removable liner ring and the KdbK has a bag-fixing hole in its bucket. The KdbK and ELPHECO both include 20 bags. Cans that solve bag slipping or supply scored higher for convenience.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: Finally we compared capacity, from the Glad at 12 gallons to the EKO Madison at 13.2, and size where listed, such as the ELPHECO at 16.7 by 14.1 inches. We weighed how well each shape suits a narrow gap against how much it holds, because a steel can is a long-term piece of kitchen furniture.

cards.label: Pedal cans
cards.text: The EKO Madison, KdbK, Glad and ELPHECO are foot-pedal cans. They are mechanical, need no batteries and quote durability figures like 200,000 uses. They require a free foot, which is awkward only if you lean on a counter. Choose a pedal for low maintenance.

cards.label: Sensor cans
cards.text: The BestOffice and Ninestars open on a wave of the hand. They need C batteries, quoted at 40,000 openings or up to nine months, and want a dry place. Their benefit is hands-free comfort and no stepping. Choose a sensor if you carry things to the bin often.

howToChoose.note: If you dislike swapping batteries, stay with a pedal can.

faq.q: Are stainless steel trash cans better than plastic ones?
faq.a: Steel resists dents and odors better and looks cleaner, but it is heavier and can show fingerprints unless brushed or matte. Plastic is lighter and cheaper but can stain. Most steel cans here, like the KdbK and ELPHECO, still use a plastic inner bucket, so you get the best of both.

faq.q: Will a stainless trash can rust?
faq.a: Quality stainless resists rust, but scratches and standing water can still cause spots at seams. Wipe up spills and dry the area around the pedal, especially on cans in wet rooms. Avoid abrasive pads. If you place a sensor can like the BestOffice, keep it dry, as the listing advises.

faq.q: How do I keep fingerprints off a steel trash can?
faq.a: Choose a brushed or matte finish, such as the EKO Madison or KdbK, and wipe it with a damp microfiber cloth, going with the grain. A dry towel is enough for light daily care on the BestOffice. Skip glass cleaners with ammonia that can streak steel.

faq.q: Is a sensor trash can worth the extra hassle?
faq.a: It depends how much you value hands-free use. The Ninestars and BestOffice open on a wave, which helps with full hands, but they need batteries and a dry spot. The Ninestars quotes up to nine months on three C batteries. If you want fewer things to maintain, a pedal can is simpler.

faq.q: What size stainless can should I buy?
faq.a: Thirteen gallons suits most households because it matches standard supermarket bags, as on the EKO Madison, KdbK and ELPHECO. The Glad at 12 gallons is fine for one to three people. If you throw out bulky packaging or cook daily, lean toward the 13-gallon models.

faq.q: How long will the pedal last?
faq.a: The EKO Madison is rated to last over 200,000 uses and the KdbK is tested 200,000 times, while the Glad and ELPHECO listings give no figure. These are maker claims, but they show what each design targets. Press the pedal with your foot normally and avoid kicking it to extend its life.

faq.q: Do I need an odor filter in a steel can?
faq.a: Not always. A tight, soft-closing lid does much of the work, and the Glad adds Clorox odor protection to its lid. The best habit is emptying food waste before it sits for days and wiping the inner bucket occasionally. A filter helps only if the lid is sealed well.
